diocese: The Episcopal Diocese of Southern Virginia
source: The Episcopal Diocese of Southern Virginia Cycle of Prayer, July 2026 – June 2027
sourceFile: Diosova.org-2026-to-2027-Diocesean-Cycle-of-Prayer.pdf (supplied directly by Josh after the diocese's own site, diosova.org, proved unreachable from this sandbox -- see notes)
notes: This diocese's own website (diosova.org) is protected by a SiteGround 'Robot Challenge Screen' JS proof-of-work bot check that defeated every fetch attempt from this sandbox (a direct curl, the WebFetch tool, and the r.jina.ai reader-proxy workaround that had succeeded on a different diocese's Cloudflare block earlier in this project) -- reported to Josh as a blocked link per his standing preference, and this PDF was then supplied directly by Josh as a file upload rather than fetched by this session.

The single source document covers a full year, July 2026 through June 2027 (52 weekly entries), split almost exactly in half by the calendar year boundary (26 weeks in 2026, 26 in 2027) -- following this corpus's established two-file-split precedent (episcopal-delaware-2026.json/-2027.json, episcopal-southeast-florida-2026.json/-2027.json) rather than the disclose-and-include-a-lead-in precedent used for a lopsided split, since this is a genuine near-even divide, not a small lead-in on either side. This file, episcopal-southern-virginia-2026.json, covers the first 26 weeks (July 5-December 27, 2026); the remaining 26 weeks (January 3-June 27, 2027) are in the companion episcopal-southern-virginia-2027.json.

Every week's paragraph follows the fixed template "In our Diocesan Cycle of Prayers, we pray for X and Y; and for Z[, ...].", where X and Y are (almost always) two named parishes and the remainder names one or more additional intentions. Two weeks break this pattern entirely: the week of July 5, 2026 names no parish at all (only the diocesan camp Chanco on the James and a civic anniversary); the week of June 27, 2027 names only ONE parish (Trinity, South Boston) rather than the usual two.

Confirmed the document is single-column, prose-per-week throughout (no multi-column layout, so none of this corpus's usual column-interleaving risk applies) by rendering all 8 pages as images and visually cross-checking every week against a pdftotext -layout extraction before transcribing.

A recurring source-side typo, preserved verbatim rather than silently corrected per this corpus's standing rule: eight parish names are printed with the comma placed BEFORE the closing/possessive apostrophe instead of after it, e.g. "St. James,’ Accomac" where a normal "St. James', Accomac" is clearly intended. This transposition recurs identically throughout the document (affecting several distinct St. James', All Saints', St. Matthias', and St. Thomas' entries across both files) and is disclosed individually on each affected subject's own `note` field rather than corrected.

Where a week's additional intention(s) are phrased as one continuous "...and for..." clause with no independent repetition of "for", it is kept as a single `category` subject; where the source instead independently reintroduces "for" (or an equivalent, like a second semicolon-separated clause) for each item, each is recorded as its own separate `category` subject. This distinction is applied consistently throughout both files and is not re-disclosed on every individual entry.
`liturgicalNote` is null throughout both files -- the source labels every entry only by its calendar date ("Week of [Month] [Day]"), never by a liturgical Sunday/season name.
All 26 dates in this file were independently verified to fall on an actual Sunday before transcription.
